note: 'the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders came to him, and they began saying to him, By what authority do you do these things?' (Mark 11:27-28). He declines to answer at 11:33.; 'And the chief priests began to accuse Him of many things' (Mark 15:3); 'And when He was accused by the chief priests and elders, He gave no answer.' (Matt 27:12).
'When the chief priests and scribes heard this, they looked for a way to kill Him.' (Mark 11:18), immediately after the temple.; Consulted, then took counsel, to put Jesus to death.

'So the chief priests made plans to kill Lazarus as well, for on account of him many of the Jews were deserting them and believing in Jesus' (John 12:10-11). **A man raised from the dead becomes evidence, and the evidence is what they move against.**
'Now My soul is troubled, and what shall I say? Father, save Me from this hour? No, it is for this purpose that I have come to this hour. Father, glorify Your name' (John 12:27-28).
'Jesus sent out two of His disciples' (Mark 11:1) to get the colt (11:2). Two of them, unnamed.; stated as purpose rather than as an act done here: "to be sent out to preach"
'Six days before the Passover, Jesus came to Bethany, the hometown of Lazarus, whom He had raised from the dead.' (John 12:1).

'The next day the great crowd that had come to the feast heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem.' (John 12:12), riding as Mark has it: 'they led the colt to Jesus ... He sat on it' (Mark 11:7), entering the city and the temple at 11:11.; Brought as an infant to be presented at the temple.; Went up with his parents every year at Passover; on this occasion, aged twelve, he stayed behind.; Went up for the Passover early in his ministry and cleansed the temple.; Went up for a feast; healed the impotent man at the pool of Bethesda.; Went up secretly for the feast (of tabernacles, per John 7:2) and taught in the temple; the verse names the feast, not the city.; At Jerusalem for the feast of dedication in winter; walked in Solomon's porch.; Entered in triumph on the colt; the whole city was moved.
'As they approached Jerusalem and came to Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent out two of His disciples' (Mark 11:1).

'Why wasn't this perfume sold for three hundred denarii and the money given to the poor?' (John 12:5), spoken by 'Judas Iscariot, who was going to betray Him' (12:4). The verse names him and describes her act without naming her, so the pair rides on 12:3 above.
'So they hosted a dinner for Jesus there. Martha served' (John 12:2) -- the same serving Luke 10:40 has her busy with.

'Then Mary took about a pint of expensive perfume, made of pure nard, and she anointed Jesus' feet and wiped them with her hair' (John 12:3). **Jesus reads the act himself**: 'She has kept this perfume in preparation for the day of My burial' (12:7), which is the text supplying its own key.
